title: What goes on the fast track
question: Which kinds of file, which departments and which committees account for the committee reports?
finding: By kind, the 206 committee reports are mostly contract or other agreement (95, 8.9% of that kind); lease, licence or concession (37, 6.0% of that kind); appropriation or budget ordinance (18, 7.2% of that kind); settlement with a business (17, 8.8% of that kind). By department: Public Health (37, $1.23 billion); Real Estate Division (22, $107.0 million); Homelessness and Supportive Housing (20, $700.3 million); Airport (10, $126.9 million); Public Utilities Commission (8, $40.9 million). By committee the share is highest at the Homelessness and Behavioral Health Select Committee, which sent 28 of its 34 files this way (82.4%). No kind or department stands out for dissent: the no votes on committee reports are spread across 4 kinds of file.
how: The same files as on the screen before, counted three ways: by kind of file, by the department the title names, and by the committee that sent the file. “All files” is every money file of that kind, department or committee with a recorded committee recommendation and final vote, so the share shows how much of each goes this way. The wait is the median number of days from the committee vote to the Board’s first vote.
limits: A committee that meets on a Thursday or Friday has to use a committee report to reach the following Tuesday’s meeting at all, so the committee’s meeting day explains much of this table. Departments with deadlines set by others, such as grant conditions and lease expiries, will appear more often. Dollar figures are the totals named in file titles: an agreement amended twice is counted at each new total, rent and accepted grants are money coming to the City as well as money going out, and budget ordinances name no single figure, so a sum of title dollars measures what the titles name, not money spent. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
